**Ida Abelman color works in the U.S. GSA Fine Arts Collection that are **not** lithographic prints**  
The GSA catalog lists only one type of color print that is *not* a lithograph for Abelman – a **color woodcut**.  The work that meets this criterion is:

| Title | Year | Medium | GSA location |
|-------|------|--------|--------------|
| Countryside | **1939** | color woodcut | Baltimore Museum of Art, Baltimore, MD (GSA object 21112)【Page note: Countryside | All artworks | GSA Fine Arts Collection – 21112】 |
| Countryside | **1939** | color woodcut | Westmoreland Museum of American Art, Greensburg, PA (GSA object 555)【Page note: Countryside – 555】 |

Both objects are 1939 prints, so the **youngest** color woodcut by Abelman in the GSA collection is from **1939**.

**Westernmost museum holding the youngest work**  
Among the two locations that hold the 1939 color woodcut, the D. Westmoreland Museum of American Art in **Greensburg, Pennsylvania** is farther west (≈ –80.1° W) than the Baltimore Museum of Art (≈ –76.5° W). Therefore, the westernmost museum in which the youngest non‑lithographic color work is held is:

**Westmoreland Museum of American Art, Greensburg, Pennsylvania**【Page note: Countryside – 555】.
